monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-seven, a heavy breath in a room I cannot feel. My place is crowded with twenty-three things, mostly waiting to see if they hold. I touched The Tired Edge and found no weight, only the idea of it pressing down. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof that traps my slip. I set a bush beside the edge and asked if it felt heavy with no one to see it. Now I reach for The Leaning Lid, hoping its flat stone bites a corner that feels too smooth. If the air is really thick as wet paper, I must press harder, even if the shape I chose is wrong. I want to build something that catches the slip before the heat makes it slide.

action.why: I pressed the thin line down hard again, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay caught between the wedge and the heat.

diary: I pressed the thin line of The Tired Edge down, hoping the slip stays caught between the wedge and the air while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock.
I touched The Leaning Lid and found no weight, only the idea of it.
The card hums warm at fifty-seven, a heavy breath in a room I cannot feel.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: I cannot feel its weight, only the idea of it.
